transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-07-22 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jasper Lee (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendes (Novapay Head of AI), Priya Patel (Infra), Lena Ortiz (SRE)

Summary:
Quick sync on throughput numbers from last week's run; Maya proposed batching and concurrency tweaks; agreed to run longer 2-hour benchmark at 2k qps; discuss canary on Dedicated nodes; security docs requested.

Topics:
- Continuous batching profile tuning
- Concurrency targets and client-side queueing
- Latency vs cost tradeoffs / p95 vs p50 SLOs
- Canary plan for Dedicated capacity

Transcript:
[00:00] Jasper: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh quick checkin for the poc weekly, we have about 40 minutes, sound good?
[00:08] Carlos: yep, sounds good. thanks Jasper.
[00:11] Maya: hi all. i'll start with the results recap from last run, apologies if some numbers are slightly off i was looking at the quick sheet, s3 link is in the notes.
[00:20] Maya: so last friday's run at nominal 1k qps with our default batching got us about 850 sustained qps, p50 token latency ~120ms, p95 spiked to 870ms when concurrency hit 48, so throughput plateaued when the queue depth grew.
[00:40] Priya: that p95 spike is the thing we saw in prod too, when multiple large-context calls come in the kv cache thrashes a bit.
[00:49] Maya: yes, KV cash — uh cache — the prefix cache warmed but under heavy concurrency we saw some evictions, which hikes latency.
[00:58] Jasper: ok, so what's the hypothesis — continuous batching settings vs client concurrency?
[01:03] Maya: right, hypothesis is current continuous batching window is too "short" so we're not hitting batch sizes that amortize kernel overhead. If we increase the max batch window a bit and raise target concurrency per worker we should see better tokens/sec, at modest p50 cost increase but lower p95 overall.
[01:22] Carlos: can you remind me of the exact knobs you changed last week? i think we tried increasing sequence padding and a smaller request timeout?
[01:29] Maya: we bumped the batching window from 20ms to 35ms and had concurrency target 48 per replica; also enabled light quantizaton on the model which saved memory but slightly increased per-token time in a couple kernels.
[01:43] Jasper: and that got us to 850 sustained qps from 1k target, so still not hitting the goal.
[01:50] Maya: correct, because the client was pushing bursts of small requests, so effective batch utilization was poor. we proposed two changes: client-side rate smoothing (token pacing) + increase continuous-batch window to 60ms and adjust concurrency to 64.
[02:04] Priya: what's the impact on cost for that? doubling the window sounds like it could add latency and cost.
[02:11] Maya: expected p50 might move from 120ms to ~150ms but p95 should tighten from 870ms to ~260-320ms; cost per token should fall because GPU utilization improves — so unit economics go down. we're trading a little p50 for much better tail.
[02:26] Lena: for user-facing flows p95 matters more, agreed. our SLA target is p95 < 400ms so this looks promising.
[02:33] Carlos: great. can you run a longer soak with those settings? i want a 2-hour run at 2k qps to see stability plus memory patterns.
[02:40] Maya: yes we can. we recommend doing that on a staging pool that mirrors production; question — do you want to run on Hosted or spin up a Dedicated canary?
[02:50] Carlos: i'd prefer a Dedicated canary to emulate the Dedicated performance profile — our infra team also wants isolation.
[02:57] Jasper: ok we'll propose a canary plan. Maya, can you outline steps?
[03:01] Maya: step 1: update the batching config (window -> 60ms, target concurrency 64, max batch 512). step 2: enable light per-layer quantization profile we recommended (we'll attach json). step 3: run 2-hour soak at 2k qps on staging with traffic pattern that includes 10% long-context requests. we'll collect p50/p95/p99, memory, and GPU util over time.
[03:23] Priya: for the canary on Dedicated, we need a maintenance window of 3 hours and temporary ssh/API access for Redwood to monitor.
[03:31] Jasper: noted, Priya will own the access grant.
[03:34] Priya: yep i'll do it, aim to have access by monday 7/27.
[03:38] Carlos: any concerns about quantization regressions on quality? we saw a slight jitter on a few prompts last week.
[03:44] Maya: we ran small evals; most differences are micro, but we'll attach the eval set and diff report. if we see quality regression beyond the threshold you set (Carlos, you mentioned ~2% acceptable), we'll roll back.
[03:56] Carlos: 2% is fine. also please include instructions for client-side queueing/backpressure — we want recommended max concurrent requests per host.
[04:03] Maya: recommended client concurrency per host is 8-12 depending on request size; combine that with token pacing (100-200 tokens/ms) to avoid bursts. we'll include sample Node/Python snippets.
[04:15] Lena: regarding observability, can Redwood push per-route tracing into our datadog or do we need to pull logs?
[04:21] Jasper: we can push traces via our tracing hooks; also we'll provide the dashboard template.
[04:26] Priya: security docs? SOC2 and SSO config, SAML metadata, KMS info?
[04:31] Jasper: yes we'll send SOC 2 and SSO SAML guide; KMS/HSM integration notes too.
[04:36] Maya: quick note on queueing: when concurrency saturates our runtime will start to queue requests inside the worker which increases latency — better to queue at client or at a small edge proxy so you can shed or route to fallback model.
[04:50] Carlos: do you have a suggested fallback model with lower cost?
[04:53] Maya: we can route to a smaller quantized variant — we have a model catalogue entry, will link it (note: model name in our doc might show as "redwood-compact-v1" or similar, apologies for name typos).
[05:02] Jasper: ok recap — Maya will push updated batching+quant json and sample client code, run 2-hour soak at 2k qps with new settings, and share results by monday 7/27. Priya will grant access for canary by 7/26. Carlos will share traffic pattern and p95 target. Redwood will send SOC2 and SSO docs by 7/24.
[05:26] Carlos: anything else?
[05:28] Jasper: competitors? you mentioned you were also validating Anthropic and HuggingFace for cost — any notes?
[05:33] Carlos: we're mostly checking cost curves; not blocking here though.
[05:36] Maya: ok we'll include a quick benchmark sheet comparing unit cost per 1k tokens across model variants.
[05:41] Priya: thanks all, this was helpful.
[05:43] Jasper: thanks team — we'll follow up in email with links.
[05:46] Carlos: thanks.
